Eulogy

YOO-luh-jee -- Greek eu- ('good, well') plus logos ('word, speech'): good words about someone. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Eulogy is a piece of spoken or written high praise.

Her essay was less a review than a eulogy for a writer she clearly adored.

Worked Example

At the end of the season the team captain stands up at the banquet and spends five minutes describing everything the retiring equipment manager has quietly done for twenty years.

A speech or piece of writing given over entirely to praise is exactly what a eulogy is. Unlike an 'introduction,' which simply presents someone, a eulogy exists to honor them.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

commendation: A commendation is official recognition of someone's worth, issued by an authority -- a general commends a soldier, a school board commends a teacher. A eulogy needs no authority behind it: it is a whole speech or piece of writing given over to praising someone, personal and warm rather than official.

compliment: A compliment is a brief, friendly remark of praise -- one nice sentence about someone's work or shoes, over in a moment. A eulogy is praise built to last: a whole speech or written piece honoring one person, the kind you draft and polish for a real occasion.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

criticism: words pointing out faults

insult: words meant to offend

Where it sits · how large and ceremonial the honoring grows — praise → eulogy → tribute

praise vs. eulogy: Praise is the everyday word and can be a single sentence, while a eulogy is a whole speech or piece of writing devoted to praising one person.

tribute vs. eulogy: Tribute is the more ceremonial word: a eulogy is praise in words, while a tribute can be a statue, a concert, or a moment of silence as easily as a speech.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — eu-

prefix — eu-: good, well (Greek)

root — -logy

root — -logy: word, speech (Greek (logos))

Put it together

Put it together: Greek eulogia meant 'good words, praise,' from eu- ('well') and logos ('word, speech') -- a eulogy is literally good words spoken about someone. The eu- prefix returns in euphoria and euphemism, and the logos root in monologue and dialogue.

Use the root in a new word: monologue

Use the root in a new word: monologue: The actor delivered a five-minute monologue without a single pause.

Root Check

Word Choice

A eulogy is most familiar as the speech given at a funeral, but the word covers any high praise, spoken or written, for the living as well as the dead. Do not confuse it with elegy, a sorrowful poem of mourning.
